name: Virginia
overview: Virginia does not sell tax liens; a city or county sells the delinquent real estate itself through a court case. The locality's tax-collecting officer (usually the treasurer) can start a judicial proceeding once taxes are still delinquent on December 31 following the second anniversary of the date they became due (sooner for some derelict or blighted property). The case runs in the circuit court of the locality, and the property is sold at a judicial sale. The owner can redeem before the date set for the sale by paying into court all taxes, penalties and interest, plus costs including publication and a reasonable attorney fee set by the court.

counties.how_to_bid: Bid in person at the live auction at the front door of the Loudoun County Courthouse in Leesburg, or submit a written bid before the auction with the deposit and required certification (bid form from the Special Commissioner). Register with county staff before bidding starts, show proof of funds for each parcel's advertised minimum deposit, and certify you own no Loudoun property with delinquent taxes or violations. Sales are subject to Circuit Court confirmation; the balance is due within 30 days after confirmation.
